title: Tug-of-War at the Sinking Mire
story: Dolgrave the Mire Strider, a long-legged swamp beast of reeds and mud, has hooked a wicker cage full of marsh-larks and is hauling it toward the bubbling sinkhole. The cage starts 240 feet from the sinkhole's edge, and Dolgrave drags it 10 feet every minute. Mr 6 grabs the rope and hauls back, pulling the cage 4 feet every minute in the other direction while he works at the knots.
question: How many minutes does Mr 6 have before the cage reaches the sinkhole?
solution: Each minute the cage really moves 10 − 4 = 6 feet toward the sinkhole.
Mr 6 has 40 minutes to untie the knots.
praise: Dividing the distance by a speed was exactly the right move — the speed just needed to be the NET pull, Dolgrave's drag minus Mr 6's haul.
hint: Dolgrave pulls one way and Mr 6 pulls the other — how far does the cage actually move in one minute?
victory: With 40 minutes and a very patient knot-picking sword, Mr 6 freed every marsh-lark at minute 39. Dolgrave hauled the empty cage into the mire and sat blinking at it, out-thought and out-tugged.
